disease: Kearns-Sayre syndrome / single large-scale mitochondrial-DNA deletion (KSS; e.g. the ~4977-bp 'common deletion')
suspended_reason: The cause is a SINGLE LARGE-SCALE DELETION of the MITOCHONDRIAL genome (mtDNA) -- most commonly the ~4977-bp 'common deletion' spanning from ND5 to ATP8, which removes SEVERAL protein-coding OXPHOS genes AND several mitochondrial tRNA genes at once -- NOT a single-gene NUCLEAR promoter switch. This GENERALISES the kit's mitochondrial-genome hold along a NEW axis -- the LESION-TYPE axis -- from POINT MUTATION to STRUCTURAL REARRANGEMENT. The mtDNA hold previously fired for two POINT mutations: LHON (protein-coding Complex I subunit genes, MT-ND4/ND1/ND6) and MELAS (a mitochondrial tRNA gene, MT-TL1) -- a within-class generalisation across mtDNA gene CLASSES. Kearns-Sayre is the THIRD mtDNA suspend and extends the class once more: the lesion is not a base substitution at all but a large contiguous DELETION of a stretch of the circular ~16.6-kb mtDNA, simultaneously deleting multiple genes and tRNAs and crippling mitochondrial protein synthesis / OXPHOS in the tissues carrying a high deletion load (the KSS triad: progressive external ophthalmoplegia + pigmentary retinopathy + onset <20 yr, with cardiac conduction block, ataxia and raised CSF protein). The same three features that suspend LHON and MELAS all apply and a fourth sharpens the point. (1) The lesion is in the MITOCHONDRIAL genome, which is transcribed as long polycistronic transcripts from the mitochondrial heavy/light-strand promoters and then processed -- there is NO nuclear-style TSS -2000..+500 promoter window from which to read a gamma switch (the kit's data path resolves NUCLEAR RefSeq promoters; mtDNA has no such promoter, and a multi-gene deletion has no single readable promoter at all). (2) Penetrance/phenotype is HETEROPLASMY- and tissue-distribution-dependent and continuous (the same single deletion produces a SPECTRUM by load and tissue: KSS, the milder isolated chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia (CPEO), or Pearson marrow-pancreas syndrome) -- a continuous, multi-outcome quantity a strand-symmetric single-promoter switch cannot capture. (3) Inheritance: single large-scale mtDNA deletions are almost always SPORADIC (arising de novo in the oocyte / early embryo), not Mendelian and (unlike point mutations) usually not maternally transmitted -- a different inheritance mode again. (4) THE NEW, SHARPER POINT vs LHON/MELAS: the lesion is a STRUCTURAL REARRANGEMENT (a large contiguous deletion removing many genes), not a point mutation in one gene -- so even the notion of 'the causal gene' dissolves: there is no single mtDNA gene, let alone a single nuclear promoter, to emerge. Kearns-Sayre therefore proves the mtDNA hold keys on the MITOCHONDRIAL-GENOME mechanism regardless of LESION TYPE -- point substitution (LHON, MELAS) OR large structural deletion (KSS) -- NOT a brand-new mechanism class but the lesion-type generalisation of the mtDNA class (the structural-rearrangement analogue of how MELAS generalised LHON across mtDNA gene classes). Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene NUCLEAR promoter DNA -> hold). Like LHON and MELAS, Kearns-Sayre is suspended NOT for lack of any intervention but purely on engine-readability: management is supportive (CoQ10 and cofactor 'mito-cocktails'; cardiac PACING is mandatory and life-saving for the conduction block that defines the syndrome; hearing aids; endocrine surveillance), and heteroplasmy-shifting / mitochondrial-replacement approaches are experimental -- but none is a single-(nuclear)-promoter switch the engine can read. An mtDNA / heteroplasmy / structural-deletion model is future work, not a single-switch emergence. (Holt 1988 Nature 331:717, deletions of mtDNA in mitochondrial myopathies; Zeviani 1988 Neurology 38:1339, KSS single large-scale mtDNA deletion.)
discipline: no analyzable single-gene DNA read -> held (author's rule). Disclosed, not dropped.
